preview.tournamentOverview: The RSM Classic is played at Sea Island Golf Club's Seaside Course, a short, accurate layout that rewards approach play and around-the-green control over raw distance. Approach 7%) and around-the-green 6%) skills dominate the model, while total strokes-gained 7%) still anchors the rankings. This event matters because it closes the fall swing and offers a final chance for players to lock in 2025 PGA Tour status.
preview.modelExplainer: Approach play carries the heaviest weight at 7%, followed by total strokes-gained at 7% and around-the-green at 6%. Off-the-tee 1%) and putting 4%) are secondary, while driving accuracy 5%), bogey avoidance 0%), and birdie/bogey ratio 0%) round out the formula. The model therefore prioritizes players who hit greens from the fairway and scramble well when they miss.
preview.pickApproach: We tier bets by model rank and power rank differential, favoring golfers inside the top 20 whose course-fit metrics exceed their overall power rank. First priority goes to players strong in approach and around-the-green; secondary bets target total SG leaders whose other stats align with the 7% approach emphasis. Exposure is capped at three golfers per tier to maintain sharp allocation.

article.title: RSM Classic 2026: Model Flags Hisatsune, Yellamaraju, Lipsky at Sea Island
article.dek: Tournament model ranks Ryo Hisatsune #1, Sudarshan Yellamaraju #2, and David Lipsky #3 for the Seaside Course.
article.introduction: The RSM Classic at Sea Island Golf Club (Seaside Course) features a 141-player field with course weights emphasizing SG APP 7%) and SG ATG 6%). The tournament model identifies Ryo Hisatsune (rank #1, 238), Sudarshan Yellamaraju (rank #2, 34), and David Lipsky (rank #3, 89) as the strongest fits. All three players carry modelRank values well ahead of their powerRank numbers and share the same post-Open research classification of skipped Scottish Open plus top-10 model rank.

sections.heading: Tournament Overview
sections.body: The RSM Classic at Sea Island Golf Club (Seaside Course) carries course weights of SG Total 7%, SG APP 7%, and SG ATG 6%. The model ranks 141 players using these weights, producing a top-20 list where Ryo Hisatsune (rank #1), Sudarshan Yellamaraju (rank #2), and David Lipsky (rank #3) occupy the first three positions.

sections.heading: Course Fit
sections.body: Seaside Course weights place the heaviest emphasis on SG APP 7%) and SG ATG 6%). Hisatsune posts 576 and 181, Yellamaraju posts 474 and 188, and Lipsky posts 192 and 524. These values align with the two highest-weighted categories.

sections.heading: Recent Form
sections.body: The model incorporates sgTotal values of 238 for Hisatsune, 34 for Yellamaraju, and 89 for Lipsky. These figures place all three players inside the top-3 of the 141-player field and ahead of their respective powerRank numbers (20, 19, 24).

sections.heading: Post-Open Workload
sections.body: All three players carry the classification NO_TRACKED_ROUNDS (0 tracked rounds) in the major swing workload column. This indicates no rounds were recorded in the tracked events and does not imply rest.

sections.heading: FedExCup Motivation
sections.body: Hisatsune enters at FedExCup rank #47 (SAFE_TOP_50), Yellamaraju at rank #58 (BUBBLE_51_80), and Lipsky at rank #85 (CHASING_81_PLUS). These standings provide differing levels of season-long pressure heading into the event.

sections.heading: Crossover Research Angles
sections.body: Each player shares the classification of skipped Scottish Open plus top-10 model rank / Tournament model rank well ahead of power rank. Hisatsune (modelRank=1 vs powerRank=20), Yellamaraju (modelRank=2 vs powerRank=19), and Lipsky (modelRank=3 vs powerRank=24) all exhibit this gap.

sections.heading: Outright Targets
sections.body: The outright tier consists of Ryo Hisatsune (model rank #1, 238) and Sudarshan Yellamaraju (model rank #2, 34). Both players sit inside the top-2 of the tournament model and carry the same crossover classification.

sections.heading: Top-10 Targets
sections.body: The top-10 tier includes Ryo Hisatsune (model rank #1), Sudarshan Yellamaraju (model rank #2), and David Lipsky (model rank #3). Lipsky adds 524, the strongest around-the-green figure among the three.

sections.heading: Top-20 Targets
sections.body: The top-20 tier mirrors the top-10 group: Hisatsune (rank #1), Yellamaraju (rank #2), and Lipsky (rank #3). All three maintain modelRank values at least 16 spots ahead of their powerRank numbers.

sections.heading: Data Limitations
sections.body: Weather and tee-time data are not available in this pipeline. The article does not make weather- or tee-time-specific claims.

sections.heading: Final Betting Card
sections.body: Outright: Ryo Hisatsune, Sudarshan Yellamaraju. Top-5: Ryo Hisatsune, Sudarshan Yellamaraju. Top-10: Ryo Hisatsune, Sudarshan Yellamaraju, David Lipsky. Top-20: Ryo Hisatsune, Sudarshan Yellamaraju, David Lipsky.

article.conclusion: Model tier: Hisatsune and Yellamaraju for outright and top-5. Secondary tier: Lipsky for top-10 and top-20. All three selections are supported by model rank, sgTotal, and crossover classification.

keyTakeaways.text: Ryo Hisatsune leads the model at rank #1 with sgTotal=1.238 and sgApp=0.576, placing him in the outright tier.
Sudarshan Yellamaraju sits at model rank #2 with sgTotal=1.34 and sgPutt=0.616, also in the outright tier.
David Lipsky ranks #3 in the model with sgTotal=0.89 and sgAtG=0.524, qualifying for top-10 and top-20 cards.
All three selections share the crossover classification of skipped Scottish Open plus top-10 model rank ahead of power rank.
